subject.title: Plugin installs crash Express 4.x routes: core npm-shrinkwrap pins path-to-regexp@8.x but no central override covers plugins

question: Should managed npm plugin installs stop inheriting host workspace overrides such as `path-to-regexp`, or should OpenClaw keep propagation and add targeted validation/guidance for incompatible plugin graphs?
rationale: The source fix is not just mechanical: changing override propagation affects third-party plugin dependency ownership, security pinning, and OpenClaw's own Express 5 dependency policy.

options.title: Scope host overrides away from plugin-owned graphs
options.body: Preserve OpenClaw-owned override policy for core/bundled packages while letting third-party plugin package ranges or shrinkwraps resolve inside their managed project root, backed by Express 4 and Express 5 regression tests.

options.title: Add validator-only detection
options.body: Detect Express 4 plus forced `path-to-regexp` 8.x during install and fail with an actionable message, leaving plugin authors responsible for package-local overrides or Express 5 migration.

options.title: Keep current propagation
options.body: Require conflicting third-party plugins to ship their own overrides or migrate dependencies, accepting the current runtime failure mode until those packages update.

recommendation.title: Scope host overrides away from plugin-owned graphs
recommendation.body: Preserve OpenClaw-owned override policy for core/bundled packages while letting third-party plugin package ranges or shrinkwraps resolve inside their managed project root, backed by Express 4 and Express 5 regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Most directly connected to the managed npm override propagation and recent plugin install dependency policy history.
